name: Approve a CSR + fix a broken binding
objective: CKA › Cluster Architecture, Installation & Configuration. Drill EVERY RBAC corner harder than the exam: namespaced Role vs cluster-scoped ClusterRole, binding to users and ServiceAccounts, reusing a ClusterRole inside one namespace via a RoleBinding, least-privilege with resourceNames, apiGroups for subresources, approving a CSR, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix. Graded exactly, per requirement.

questions.title: Approve a CertificateSigningRequest
questions.teach:
A **CertificateSigningRequest** lets an admin issue a client cert to a new user. List pending ones with `kubectl get csr`, then grant one with `kubectl certificate approve <name>`; its condition then reads `Approved,Issued`.

**Gotcha:** approval only proves identity — it grants **no** permissions without a Role/ClusterRole binding.
questions.prompt:
The CSR `learn-dev` is already submitted and **Pending**. Approve it.

Target: `kubectl get csr learn-dev` shows condition `Approved,Issued`.
questions.hint: `kubectl get csr` to see it Pending, then `kubectl certificate approve learn-dev`.
questions.solution:
kubectl get csr
kubectl certificate approve learn-dev
kubectl get csr learn-dev   # Approved,Issued

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a binding that grants nothing
questions.teach:
When `auth can-i` says `no` despite a RoleBinding existing, suspect a **dangling roleRef**: the binding points at a Role name that doesn't exist, so it grants nothing silently. Check with `kubectl -n <ns> describe rolebinding <name>`.

**Gotcha:** a RoleBinding's `roleRef` is **immutable** — to repoint it you must delete and recreate the binding.
questions.prompt:
User `auditor` should be able to `get,list` `secrets` in `rbac-learn`, but `kubectl auth can-i list secrets --as=auditor -n rbac-learn` returns `no`. A Role `secret-reader` (correct rules) and a RoleBinding `auditor-sr` already exist — the binding is misconfigured. Diagnose and fix it so `auditor` can list secrets. Don't change the Role's rules; fix the wiring.

Target: `kubectl auth can-i list secrets --as=auditor -n rbac-learn` → `yes`.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n rbac-learn describe rolebinding auditor-sr` — its `roleRef` points at a Role that doesn't exist. Since roleRef is immutable, delete and recreate: `kubectl -n rbac-learn delete rolebinding auditor-sr` then `kubectl -n rbac-learn create rolebinding auditor-sr --role=secret-reader --user=auditor`.
questions.solution:
# describe shows roleRef -> Role 'secret-readr' (typo); no such Role, so it grants nothing.
kubectl -n rbac-learn delete rolebinding auditor-sr
kubectl -n rbac-learn create rolebinding auditor-sr --role=secret-reader --user=auditor
kubectl auth can-i list secrets --as=auditor -n rbac-learn   # -> yes

verification.description: auditor can list secrets in rbac-learn (dangling roleRef fixed)
